record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Polyomino Tilings
record.context_brief: Finite-region tiling complexity for tileable polyominoes
record.original_question: Fix a polyomino P that does tile the plane. Is the decision problem 'does P tile at least one finite region?' NP-hard for every such P?

evidence.quote: The algorithmic problems of determining whether a given polyomino can tile a finite region have been shown to be NP-complete for the L-tromino and square (i.e., 2× 2) tetromino

these problems are closely related to the NP-hard problem of exact set cover in planar graphs ... and thus are likely NP-complete for all larger polyominoes as well. However, the author is not aware of any proof of such a result.
Open Problem 10 (Hinted at by [29]) For every polyomino P that has a plane tiling, is determining whether P can tile a finite region NP-hard?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polyomino is a finite, edge-connected union of unit squares in the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$, considered up to translation (and, when desired, rotations and reflections). A polyomino $P$ is said to tile the plane if there exists a covering of $\mathbb{R}^2$ by non-overlapping isometric copies of $P$ (allowing translations, rotations, and reflections of $P$). A finite region is a finite, simply or non-simply connected union of unit squares of $\mathbb{Z}^2$; we say $P$ tiles such a region $R$ if $R$ can be partitioned into non-overlapping isometric copies of $P$.

For each polyomino $P$ that tiles the plane, consider the decision problem
$$\mathrm{TILE}_P:\ \text{given a finite region } R \subset \mathbb{Z}^2 \text{ as input, decide whether } R \text{ can be tiled by isometric copies of } P.$$

It is known that $\mathrm{TILE}_P$ is NP-complete when $P$ is the L-tromino and when $P$ is the $2\times 2$ square tetromino.

Question: Is it true that for every polyomino $P$ which admits a tiling of the plane, the decision problem $\mathrm{TILE}_P$ is NP-hard?
artifact.status_search_result: A search did not turn up a proof establishing NP-hardness of the finite-region tiling problem for every plane-tileable polyomino. NP-completeness is known for specific small polyominoes (e.g., L-tromino, 2×2 square) and for the related problem of tiling one polyomino with another (Moore–Robson, 2001), but the universal statement appears not to have been proved. No source indicating resolution was found, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Polyomino - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: In 2001 Cristopher Moore and John Michael Robson showed that the problem of tiling one polyomino with copies of another is NP-complete.
status_evidence.claim: NP-completeness is known for specific tiling problems, but a general result for every plane-tileable polyomino is not reported.

status_evidence.title: Tiling with Squares and Packing Dominos in Polynomial Time
status_evidence.snippet: Tiling with squares and packing dominos in polynomial time.
status_evidence.claim: Some specific cases are tractable, indicating no uniform NP-hardness theorem is known for all plane-tileable polyominoes.
